items.name: Niger seed (ramtil)
items.prabhava: The Deccan chutney seed — gurellu/karale podi country cooking; warming oil-seed of dryland farms.
combinations: gurellu chutney powder with garlic and chili
items.preparation: Dry-roast until aromatic before grinding — raw niger tastes flat; the roast wakes it.

items.name: Tulsi seed
items.prabhava: Holy basil's seed swells like sabja into cooling gel — paradoxical child of a heating plant; used in sherbets like its sweet-basil cousin.
items.preparation: Soak 15 minutes; market 'sabja' is usually sweet-basil seed — true tulsi seed is smaller and scarcer.
items.reviewNote: Market conflation with sabja (dravya.sabja-seed, sweet basil) is near-universal; expert to confirm keeping both.

items.name: Buffalo milk
items.prabhava: Classical texts mark mahisha milk as heavier and colder than cow's — sleep-promoting (nidrakara) and deeply building; India's majority milk.
combinations: boiled with dry ginger or cardamom (necessary lightening)
the traditional base of khoya, paneer and rich chai
items.preparation: Always boiled with a warming spice; its classical gift is deep sleep — take it at night, not before work.

items.name: Camel milk
items.prabhava: The desert exception among milks — classically light, slightly salty and heating; the one milk that scrapes rather than builds kapha.
combinations: fresh as the Raika herders take it
contraindications: classical texts reserve it for specific conditions
items.preparation: Traditionally drunk fresh; its lightness makes it the classical choice where other milks clog.

items.name: Sheep milk
combinations: mostly as cheese and yogurt in world cuisines
contraindications: classical texts rank avi ksheera low among milks
items.preparation: Richest in fat and protein of common milks; classical texts treat it warily — cheese and yogurt are its better destinations.

items.name: Khoya (mawa)
items.prabhava: Milk reduced to a solid — the concentrated heart of Indian sweets; kilata-class density that demands festival portions and strong agni.
combinations: base of barfi, gulab jamun, gujiya
small portions with cardamom and nuts
contraindications: adulteration-prone market item — source carefully at festivals
items.preparation: Slow-reduce full milk to a fudgy mass; festival food by design — the density that makes sweets divine makes daily use unwise.

items.name: Chhena (fresh curd cheese)
items.prabhava: Bengal's moist acid-set cheese — the crumbly soul of rasgulla and sandesh; fresher and lighter than pressed paneer.
combinations: kneaded into sandesh with date jaggery
contraindications: eat fresh — it sours within a day unrefrigerated
items.preparation: Curdle hot milk with lime, drain briefly without pressing — moisture is what separates chhena from paneer.

items.name: Hung curd (chakka)
items.prabhava: Yogurt with its whey drained away — dadhi concentrated; the shrikhand base, thicker and heavier than the curd it came from.
viruddha: with fruit in the same bowl (traditional caution)
items.preparation: Hang fresh curd in muslin 4–6 hours; all yogurt rules apply with extra weight — the whey that drained off carried the lightness.

items.name: Whey (mastu)
items.prabhava: Mastu is the classical light fraction of curd — praised as digestive, channel-clearing and strength-giving without heaviness; the liquid most kitchens pour away.
combinations: salted with roasted cumin as a drink
items.preparation: Save the liquid from paneer-making or curd-straining; classical texts value what modern kitchens discard.

items.name: Colostrum milk
items.prabhava: The first post-calving milk — piyusha; immunoglobulin-dense building substance that tradition steams into kharvas rather than drinking raw.
items.preparation: Cook thoroughly — the traditional steamed pudding is both the safety protocol and the delicacy.

items.name: Buffalo ghee
items.prabhava: The white ghee of buffalo milk — heavier and colder than cow ghee; classical texts consistently rank cow ghrita above it for medicine, buffalo for bulk richness.
contraindications: prefer cow ghee for daily and medicinal use (classical ranking)
items.preparation: Distinguish by color — buffalo ghee is white, cow ghee golden; use where richness matters more than lightness.

items.name: Skimmed milk
combinations: warmed with spices (the rules don't change)
where fat restriction is medically directed
contraindications: vata (fat removed = grounding removed — whole milk serves vata better)
items.preparation: Ayurvedically a compromise: lighter for kapha, but stripped of the sneha that makes milk nourishing — boil with spices as usual.

items.name: Full-cream milk (packaged)
items.prabhava: Homogenized-pasteurized whole milk — the packaged everyday form; treat by all classical milk rules, boiled with spices before drinking.
viruddha: fish, salt, sour fruit, banana, yogurt (milk rules)
contraindications: often buffalo-cow blend in India — composition varies
items.preparation: Boil once with a warming spice even though pasteurized — the samskara is digestive, not just microbial.
items.reviewNote: Fresh cow milk exists as dravya.milk-cow (batch 01); this is the packaged full-cream commercial form users actually log.

items.name: Milk powder
contraindications: Ayurvedic view: a processed shadow of milk — fresh milk always preferred
items.preparation: Reconstitute warm and spice as milk; better as an ingredient in sweets than a daily milk replacement.

usda.name: Milk, dry, whole, without added vitamin D

items.name: Condensed milk, sweetened
items.preparation: Milk and sugar reduced together — dessert concentrate; measure in spoons and treat as festival material.

items.name: Rice bran oil
items.prabhava: The neutral modern Indian cooking oil — high smoke point, mild character; oryzanol content drives its heart-marketing.
combinations: where a flavorless oil is wanted
contraindications: refined-oil moderation (rotate with ghee, sesame, coconut)
items.preparation: Serviceable and stable; Ayurvedically characterless — fine as the neutral workhorse, not the whole story.

items.name: Castor oil (dietary)
items.inedibleReason: stimulant laxative — a drug dose, not a cooking oil
items.prabhava: Eranda taila is the classical vata medicine among oils — the gentle purgative and joint ally; a teaspoon is therapy, a tablespoon is an event.
combinations: a teaspoon in warm milk or ginger tea (traditional occasional laxative)
regional: a spoon with rice at the start of certain meals (Telangana tradition)
items.preparation: Food-medicine boundary item: occasional teaspoon doses in the traditional manner; never a cooking oil.

items.name: Almond oil (dietary)
items.prabhava: Badam rogan tradition — drops in warm milk for brain, eyes and chronic dryness; the luxury oil taken by the spoon, not the pan.
combinations: a teaspoon in warm milk at night (badam rogan doodh)
contraindications: food-grade sweet almond only (bitter almond oil is toxic)
items.preparation: Use food-grade sweet almond oil in teaspoon doses; the traditional vehicle is warm milk before bed.
provenance: Vatada lineage; Unani-Ayurvedic badam rogan tradition

items.name: Walnut oil
items.prabhava: Omega-3 finishing oil with walnut's nerve-nourishing signature — fragile like flax oil, never heated.
combinations: drizzled over warm grains and roasted vegetables
items.preparation: Cold use only; buy small, keep cold, finish fast.
